:::{#def-affine-map}
#### Affine map (affine transformation, affine function)

A [function](functions.qmd#def-function) $f: \reals^p \to \reals^m$ is an **affine map**
(also called an **affine transformation** or **affine function**)
if it is a matrix product followed by a translation (@def-translation)
(a [composition](functions.qmd#def-composition), with the matrix product as the inner function):
there are an $m \times p$ matrix $\matr{A}$ and a vector $\vec{b} \in \reals^m$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(\vx)
&= t_{\vec{b}}(\matr{A} \vx) \\
&= \matr{A} \vx + \vec{b} \quad \text{for all } \vx \in \reals^p
\end{aligned}
$$

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#def-affine-offset}
#### Offset (intercept, bias) of an affine map

In @def-affine-map, the vector $\vec{b}$ is called the **offset** of $f$
(statistics also calls it the **intercept**, and machine learning the **bias**).

:::
